options.text: Reapplies your branch's commits on top of <base> as new commits, giving a linear history
Creates a merge commit joining two branches
Uploads your branch to the remote

questions.explanation: Rebase replays your commits onto a new base, creating new commits (new hashes) and a straight-line history — unlike merge, which adds a merge commit.

questions.prompt: What is the Golden Rule of Rebasing?

options.text: Never rebase commits that exist outside your repository (shared/pushed history)
Rebase main into every branch daily

questions.explanation: Because rebasing rewrites commits, doing it to commits others may already have breaks their history. Rebase private branches; leave shared history alone.

questions.prompt: Which are things interactive rebase (git rebase -i) can do? Select all that apply.

options.text: Rewrite history while keeping all the original commit hashes

questions.explanation: Interactive rebase can squash, reword, reorder, edit, and drop commits — but any change rewrites the commits, so the hashes change.

questions.prompt: To start an interactive rebase of the last three commits, run: git rebase -__ HEAD~3
questions.explanation: git rebase -i HEAD~3 opens the interactive editor listing the last three commits for you to pick/squash/reword/drop.

questions.prompt: You rebased your own feature branch that was already pushed, and now `git push` is rejected. What's the safe way to update the remote branch?

options.text: git push --force-with-lease (refuses if the remote changed unexpectedly)
git pull, which will duplicate the commits

questions.explanation: --force-with-lease updates your rebased branch but refuses if someone else pushed new commits you haven't seen — a safer force. Use it only on your own branch, never on shared branches like main.

questions.prompt: Match each interactive-rebase action to its effect.

pairs.right: Keep the commit but change its message

questions.explanation: pick keeps, squash combines with the prior commit, reword edits the message, and drop deletes the commit.
